title: Cord factor (TDM) as a named glycolipid
dek: Trehalose dimycolate. Wikipedia virulence-lipid node. Envelope context stays on tb-cell-envelope / tb-mycolates.
story: Cord factor on Wikipedia is trehalose dimycolate (TDM): a surface glycolipid associated with serpentine cording in culture and with granuloma/virulence folklore in older literature.
Cording is a lab-morphology hint, not a DST and not a proof of Mtb sensu stricto (other mycobacteria can cord).
Modern envelope teaching treats TDM as one extractable outer lipid among PDIM, SL-1, LAM. Do not let a 1950s 'the virulence factor' headline erase that list.
deep: PDIM has its own Simplfy plate for virulence and detergent resistance.
Granuloma induction stories in animal models are not human dosing rules.
INH-stressed cells may look morphologically odd; that is not a TDM assay.
